newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields fall sharply, crown stronger.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields fall sharply, crown stronger.

text.p: Swedish bond yields fell sharply on Thursday, mostly taking their cues from international markets.
Figures showing that U.S. jobless claims decreased less than expected and a lower than expected Swedish 1996 borrowing requirement strengthened the market.
Although higher than expected U.S. PPI figures made yields edge somewhat higher temporarily, they quickly dropped to even lower levels than before the release.
"Sweden has showen strength today but there is tension before U.S. unemployment figures on Friday," one dealer said.
"The figures can rock the world," one dealer said.
The nine-year bond yield dropped ten basis points to 6.72 percent, while the six-month T-bill rate fell five to 3.72.
The crown strengthened, especially against mark, after a period of weakness, trading at 4.3930 a mark versus 4.4295 late on Wednesday.
"However, I think there is going to be some kind of return to the level of 4.4200 crowns to the mark," a dealer said.
Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, left rates unchanged after its board meeting, meeting market expectations.
